title: The Year Begins with Thee
description: The Year Begins with Thee in Tonic Solfa to FRANCONIA, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: John Keble wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 175.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to FRANCONIA; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The year be-gins with Thee, And Thou be-gin’st with woe To let the world of sin-ners see That blood for sin must flow.

lines: To let the world of sinners see
That blood for sin must flow.
Are not enough; the legal sword
Seemeth it sad, my soul, to thee
I look, and hold my peace:
E’en from His birth takes no release
That I may reap in love,
Help me to sow in fear;
So life a winter’s morn may prove

licence: Public domain: John Keble died in 1866.
credits: Words by John Keble (1792–1866), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to FRANCONIA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
